intent: Three items from the operator's second live Hermes QA pass, 2026-08-29. A2 reported that the skills category dedup had regressed; refuted, but chasing it found a real defect in the code T-0037 shipped. B6 asked for a boot line naming the operational flags, after three sessions were lost to a watchdog restarting the server without their environment and one finding had to be retracted because of it. And an inconsistency found while refuting A5: useInterval catch-up ticks on tab return while the query layer had refetchOnWindowFocus off, so the two disagreed in the opposite direction from what useInterval's own comment claims. Closed 2026-08-29.
invariants: I1 A category heading does not depend on catalogue order. Asserted by grouping the same four spellings in two different orders and comparing the rendered heading, not by inspecting the fold.
I2 The module's stated invariant still holds: titleCaseCategory(raw).toLowerCase() === the grouping key, for every spelling. A heading and its bucket cannot drift apart again.
I3 A separator-free spelling KEEPS its own bucket. This is the thing the report asked to be changed, and changing it would reintroduce order-dependent headings by merging labels that do not match.
I4 The boot line never prints a secret. It is meant to be pasted into a bug report; the mutation that adds a token to it turns the guard red.
I5 The boot line prints unconditionally. A diagnostic that appears only when something is wrong cannot be used to establish that nothing is.
oracle_provenance: Authored BEFORE any production file was opened for edit and committed on its own at c660f814, ahead of the implementation at 85c1aa28. Two files. category-label-is-deterministic measured against dev@0ec7b9ba: 3 red, 3 green, and the greens are load-bearing because they assert the REPORTED claim is not a bug. boot-says-how-it-is-configured: module absent, so all 8 red on resolution.
verification: Four mutations against the committed implementation, tree restored and confirmed clean after each: restoring the old title-casing turns 4 red; making the boot line stop reading read-only turns 2 red; adding a token to the boot line turns 1 red; dropping the legacy CH_ alias turns 1 red. The boot line was also verified on a real server booted with PS_READ_ONLY=1 and a gateway override, and printed exactly the intended line.
report_claim_refuted: A2 said CONTROL HUB and CONTROLHUB rendering as separate rows is a regression in the T-0037 dedup. It is not. CONTROLHUB has no separator, so it title-cases to Controlhub, a different label, and the module states that a spelling which renders differently keeps its own bucket, because merging labels that do not match is what makes a heading depend on data order. The shipped seed catalogue is also clean (all lowercase single words), so the CONTROLHUB row is the operator's own skill directory naming, not shipped data.
claim_retired_by_measurement: The advertised PORT was reported as derived from `process.env.PORT ?? "3000"` rather than from the -p flag. True of the source and false of the behaviour: Next assigns process.env.PORT at bind time, before instrumentation runs. Measured on a real server booted with `-p 3494` and no PORT in the environment; the boot line advertised 3494. No fix was made. I had already carried the claim into the QA prompt as a footgun and corrected it there, which is the part worth recording: a wrong warning in a brief costs the next tester an hour looking for a bug that is not there.
pinned_defect_corrected: tests/unit/skills-category-normalization.test.ts asserted titleCaseCategory('CONTROL  HUB') === 'CONTROL HUB' and carried a comment accurately DESCRIBING the defect as though it were a design: 'titleCaseCategory raises the first letter of each word and leaves the rest alone'. Corrected in place with the reason written beside it. The merge that test protects is unchanged; what changed is that its stated premise is now true of all four spellings rather than three.
cost_accepted: Lower-casing the remainder title-cases acronyms too, so MLOps renders Mlops. The module already documented that stance for the lowercase spelling, and a heading that flickers between Control Hub and CONTROL HUB depending on which row came back first is worse than one that is consistently plain. Recorded as a judgement so a future reader can overturn it on evidence rather than guess at intent.
rollback: Revert 85c1aa28. Both oracles at c660f814 then go red again.
deferred: The boot line names five flags. PS_DATA_DIR and the resolved database path are arguably as load-bearing (the paths module already warns separately when a sibling data dir shadows the one in use), and a build id would answer 'which build is running', which the product review asked for. Both need a decision about how much boot noise is right, so they are not smuggled in here.

refetchOnWindowFocus is now on globally. staleTime keeps it cheap, but a surface with an expensive read may want to opt out per query; nothing does today, so no opt-out was invented for a caller that does not exist.
